queue.construct: if (!force and ...) / else if (redo.len == 0 and ...)  // rejects a repeated --force or --redo as a usage error
queue.reason: This only checks argument shape. No I/O boundary is involved. AC-10 asks for exit 2 on no folder, an unknown flag and --redo without a value. A repeated flag appears only in requirement.md's Assumed list, not in any AC. Dropping the two guards means a repeated --force does nothing extra and a later --redo wins.
queue.riskIfWrong: `--force --force` and `--redo a --redo b` would run the command instead of exiting 2. The AC-10 test case `{path, "--force", "--force"}` (test/cli_translate.zig:764) would have to go, and the assumption would need the owner to drop it.

queue.construct: prompt_names.get(lang) orelse return fail(w, "{s}: no prompt name", .{lang})
queue.reason: This guards data that is already parsed: the server's language list checked against a compile-time table with one entry. Config rules.io_boundaries does not list the project's own server lists. No AC covers it and no test sends a translate-1 language other than pt-BR. It is there only in case the server adds a language. The only basis is the Assumed entry 'A translate 1 language without a prompt name stops the command'.
queue.riskIfWrong: If the server starts listing a second translate-1 language (es, say) before prompt_names gains it, `.?` would panic instead of printing one line and exiting 1. If kept, it needs an AC naming that exit.

queue.construct: (lists[3].get(redo) orelse [2]u8{ 0, 0 })[1] != 1) return fail(w, "--redo {s}: not a language with translate 1", ...)
queue.reason: This validates a CLI argument against the parsed lists. It does not guard an I/O boundary. AC-7 requires it, though ('--redo it or --redo xx exits 1 and sends no OpenCode request'), and test/cli_translate.zig:661 checks it. This is a classification only. It is not a deletion proposal.
queue.riskIfWrong: Deleting it breaks AC-7: `--redo xx` would run as a no-op translate and `--redo it` would go on to moderation.
